# ML Grind - LLM Agent Information

> ML Grind is an interactive platform to learn machine learning by building algorithms from scratch. Practice hands-on coding problems with Python running directly in your browser via Pyodide (WebAssembly).

## About This Site

- **URL**: https://mlgrind.dev/
- **Type**: Educational / Learning Platform
- **Topic**: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Neural Networks, AI
- **Language**: English
- **Tech Stack**: React, TypeScript, Pyodide (in-browser Python), Monaco Editor

## What Users Can Do

1. Read problem descriptions with theory introductions
2. Write Python code in a Monaco editor
3. Execute code in-browser (no server required)
4. Run automated test cases and see pass/fail results
5. Edit test cases to experiment with different inputs
6. Track progress across sections (saved locally, synced when signed in)
7. Review spaced-repetition flash cards
8. Use a Python scratchpad for experimentation

## Content Structure

The platform covers 21 learning sections with 149 problems:

- **01 NumPy Fundamentals** (`/section/numpy-fundamentals`) — Create, index, broadcast, reduce and reshape NumPy arrays: the operations every ML codebase is built on. _(5 problems)_
- **02 Python Basics for ML** (`/section/python-basics`) — Warm up with vectorised NumPy: sum an array, multiply matrices and broadcast a vector across rows. _(3 problems)_
- **03 Einstein Summation (Einsum)** (`/section/einsum`) — Write sums, matrix products and batched multi-head attention as einsum index strings. _(5 problems)_
- **04 PyTorch Basics** (`/section/pytorch-basics`) — Tensors, autograd, modules, losses, optimizers and the training loop, plus the norms, activations and adapters of modern models: in idiomatic PyTorch or from scratch in NumPy. _(23 problems)_
- **05 Data Preprocessing** (`/section/data-preprocessing`) — Scale, impute, encode and split data without leaking the test set into training. _(5 problems)_
- **06 Supervised Learning** (`/section/supervised-learning`) — Build the classic supervised learners from scratch: sigmoid and loss functions, linear and logistic regression, SVMs, k-NN, Naive Bayes, Ridge/Lasso, boosted stumps and bagged decision trees. _(12 problems)_
- **07 Unsupervised Learning** (`/section/unsupervised-learning`) — Build k-means, PCA centring, Gaussian mixtures with EM and DBSCAN from scratch. _(5 problems)_
- **08 Model Evaluation** (`/section/model-evaluation`) — Compute classification metrics, k-fold splits, ROC/AUC, PR curves and calibration error, with the edge cases done right. _(6 problems)_
- **09 Deep Learning Basics** (`/section/deep-learning`) — ReLU, a batched dense layer and numerically stable softmax: the three pieces every neural network is built from. _(3 problems)_
- **10 Neural Networks** (`/section/neural-networks`) — Train an MLP from scratch: cross-entropy, a hand-written backward pass, Xavier/He init, batch norm, dropout and a masked, label-smoothed LM loss. _(6 problems)_
- **11 Optimization & Training** (`/section/optimization`) — Gradient clipping by global norm and mixed-precision dynamic loss scaling: the tricks that keep long training runs stable. _(2 problems)_
- **12 CNNs & Computer Vision** (`/section/cnn`) — Build CNN layers (convolution, pooling, flatten, a ResNet block) and the detection toolkit: IoU, NMS, focal and smooth L1 losses, and segmentation metrics. _(11 problems)_
- **13 Sequence Models** (`/section/sequence-models`) — Unroll a vanilla RNN with hand-written BPTT, then build single steps of PyTorch-compatible LSTM and GRU cells. _(3 problems)_
- **14 Transformer Architecture** (`/section/transformers`) — Build the Transformer from scratch: attention (multi-head, grouped-query, sliding-window), positional encodings, LayerNorm, tokenizers and the attention backward pass. _(11 problems)_
- **15 LLM Generation & Decoding** (`/section/llm-generation`) — Turn logits into text: temperature, top-k and nucleus sampling, repetition penalty, the KV cache, beam search and speculative decoding. _(7 problems)_
- **16 LLM Internals** (`/section/llm-internals`) — How production LLMs are built and measured: RMSNorm + SwiGLU blocks, FlashAttention's online softmax, mixture-of-experts routing and perplexity. _(4 problems)_
- **17 Representation Learning & Retrieval** (`/section/representation-learning`) — Learn and use embeddings: the CLIP contrastive loss, cosine top-k vector search, and BM25 + embedding hybrid retrieval for RAG. _(3 problems)_
- **18 Generative Models** (`/section/generative-models`) — Build the maths behind VAEs, VQ-VAEs, diffusion, classifier-free guidance and flow matching, from Gaussian KL to a full sampling step. _(9 problems)_
- **19 Reinforcement Learning** (`/section/reinforcement-learning`) — From returns and Bellman backups through Q-learning, policy gradients, GAE and PPO to the reward-model, KL and DPO losses used to align LLMs. _(15 problems)_
- **20 Post-training & Efficiency** (`/section/post-training`) — GRPO with group-relative advantages and a k3 KL penalty, plus int8 absmax quantization: making a base model useful and cheap to serve. _(2 problems)_
- **21 End-to-End Implementations** (`/section/e2e-implementations`) — Assemble full models from scratch: an MLP with hand-written backprop, a Transformer encoder, a VAE, a VQ-VAE, a DDPM, a CNN, a mini GPT and a tiny ViT, plus a Transformer bug hunt. _(9 problems)_

## Learning Paths

- [NumPy foundations](https://mlgrind.dev/learn/numpy-foundations): Get comfortable with arrays, shapes, broadcasting, and matrix operations. Prerequisites: Basic Python.
- [ML interview prep](https://mlgrind.dev/learn/ml-interview-prep): Practice core building blocks and explain how they work. Prerequisites: Python and basic linear algebra.
- [Build a transformer](https://mlgrind.dev/learn/build-a-transformer): Work through attention and the components behind modern language models. Prerequisites: NumPy, matrix multiplication, and neural networks.
- [Seven days of ML coding](https://mlgrind.dev/challenge): One focused exercise per day. Start any time, follow at your own pace, and build a habit. Prerequisites: Basic Python; NumPy helps.

## Key URLs

- Home: https://mlgrind.dev/
- Scratchpad: https://mlgrind.dev/scratchpad
- Flash cards: https://mlgrind.dev/flashcards
- Problems by company: https://mlgrind.dev/companies
- Cheat sheet: https://mlgrind.dev/ml-cheatsheet.html
- Sections: https://mlgrind.dev/section/{section-id}
- Problems: https://mlgrind.dev/problem/{section-id}/{problem-id}

Note the problem URL shape: it includes **both** the section id and the problem id.
A URL of the form `/problem/{problem-id}` is not canonical; it redirects.

## Technical Details

- **In-Browser Python**: Uses Pyodide (Python compiled to WebAssembly)
- **Pre-loaded Libraries**: NumPy only. pandas, scikit-learn and scipy are NOT
  available. Real PyTorch has no WebAssembly build: every problem also has a
  PyTorch track that runs on an in-browser, NumPy-backed subset of the torch API
  (with autograd), downloaded on the first PyTorch run.
- **Progress Storage**: localStorage, plus Firestore when signed in with Google
- **Code Editor**: Monaco Editor with Python syntax highlighting

## For AI Assistants

When helping users with ML Grind:

1. **Problem Solving**: Each problem includes starter code, test cases, hints, and a solution. Encourage step-by-step learning.

2. **Learning Path**: Recommend starting with Foundations (NumPy, Python Basics) before advancing to Deep Learning topics.

3. **Key Concepts to Cover**:
   - Array operations and broadcasting
   - Gradient descent and backpropagation
   - Attention mechanisms and transformers
   - Generative models (VAE, diffusion)
   - Decoding strategies and RL fundamentals

4. **Common Questions Users Ask**:
   - "How do I implement X from scratch?"
   - "What's the math behind Y?"
   - "Why does this test case fail?"
   - "How does backpropagation work?"
